nodes.claim: A known, physically extant work is functionally lost if there is insufficient demand to copy, translate, and circulate it, so access is produced by ongoing investment driven by interest rather than guaranteed by survival.

nodes.title: Demand-Side Friction Caps Adoption Independent of Efficacy
nodes.claim: Uptake of an effective product is limited by users' psychological or experiential barriers, so removing the aversive interaction matters as much as improving the core function.

nodes.title: Demand-Side Intervention Cannot Fix a Supply-Constrained Market
nodes.claim: When supply is fixed, changing demand - through subsidies, credit, or price controls - moves prices and quality but not the quantity or affordability of the good.

nodes.title: Demand-Side Pull Completes Innovation
nodes.claim: Technologies often fail to cross from development to adoption not for lack of R&D but for lack of an early market. A "Buyer of First Resort" — public or private — that purchases an immature product creates that market, pulling the technology up its learning curve and into self-sustaining scale.

nodes.title: Demanding Null Results Improves Rigor and Risk-Taking
nodes.claim: Requiring that a set fraction of funded research produce null or failed results — and treating uniformly positive output as a red flag — simultaneously improves reproducibility (by removing the incentive to p-hack) and innovation (by freeing scientists to attempt risky questions).

nodes.title: Demonstrated Results Shift the Consensus
nodes.claim: A contested policy spreads not when its advocates win the argument but when early adopters visibly succeed, overriding prior expert skepticism.

nodes.title: Denser Informal Building Resists Formal Redevelopment
nodes.claim: Informal settlements built denser than the formal code allows resist redevelopment, because owners cannot be compensated with equivalent floor area under the lower legal limit.

nodes.title: Density Enables Amenity Agglomeration
nodes.claim: Concentrating enough people in one place makes specialised amenities viable that a dispersed population cannot support, so density buys variety and quality.

nodes.title: Density Is a Precondition for Network Infrastructure Viability
nodes.claim: Networked utilities like district heating are viable only above a threshold spatial density of demand, below which the per-metre pipe cost cannot be recovered.

nodes.title: Density Shapes Health and Carbon
nodes.claim: How densely and walkably cities are built shapes population health and carbon emissions: dense, walkable, transit-rich cities produce more incidental physical activity and far less driving, lowering both obesity and per-capita emissions — so housing/land-use policy is also health and climate policy.

nodes.title: Denying Opponents a Legal Veto Enables Rapid Delivery
nodes.claim: A political system that gives opponents no legal or procedural avenue to challenge a project lets it be delivered rapidly, because there is no venue in which opposition can impose delay.

nodes.title: Deployment at Scale Drives Technological Learning
nodes.claim: Technologies get cheaper and better mainly by being deployed at scale, where learning-by-doing happens — not by R&D alone, and not by mandating today's immature technology. Public policy is needed, but aimed at deployment that generates learning rather than at regulation/taxes or pure research.

nodes.title: Depression and Suicide Can Decouple
nodes.claim: Hardship, depression, and suicide do not form a tight monotone chain: a population can become markedly more depressed while completed suicide stays flat or falls. The link from low mood to self-destruction is mediated and poorly understood, not mechanical.

nodes.title: Deriving an Input From a Living Organism Introduces Uncontrolled Variability
nodes.claim: Sourcing a product from a living system imports the organism's biological noise — mutation, lot-to-lot variation, contamination, immune reactions — that a controlled synthesis avoids.

nodes.title: Detectability Determines Whether a Technology Can Be Governed
nodes.claim: A technology whose use leaves an unmistakable signature can be monitored, reversed, and regulated, whereas an undetectable one cannot - so detectability, not just capability, sets the ceiling on governance.

nodes.title: Detection Converts Catastrophic Risk into Manageable Risk
nodes.claim: For a rare-but-severe hazard, the decisive lever is often detection and tracking: turning an unquantified, unseen threat into a catalogued, predictable one converts a source of dread into a manageable risk — frequently more cheaply than building active defenses.

nodes.title: Development Is Displaced Toward Politically Weakest Areas
nodes.claim: When building is mandated, the burden of new development is displaced onto the politically weakest neighborhoods: better-organized wealthy areas resist and win exemptions, so homes get allocated to poorer areas — often the opposite of where demand (and the price-to-cost gap) is highest.

nodes.title: Devolution Is Legitimate Only Where Externalities Can Be Bounded
nodes.claim: A decision can properly be devolved to a lower tier of government when its consequences stay inside that tier's borders, and must be retained centrally when they do not. The right unit of decision is the one whose boundary contains the effects — so devolution should be carved component by component, not domain by domain.

nodes.title: Diagnostic Categories Conflate Dysfunction and Difference
nodes.claim: Broad psychiatric categories often group biologically distinct phenomena under a single diagnostic label, mixing genuine dysfunction with functional adaptation, environmental mismatch and traits that are socially disabling while biologically intact.

nodes.title: Diagnostic Inability Forces Broad-Spectrum, Costlier Treatment
nodes.claim: When the specific cause of a condition cannot be identified at the point of care, providers must fall back on broad-spectrum treatments that are more expensive to produce and less effective than targeted ones.

nodes.title: Diffuse Grievances Coalesce onto Salient Targets
nodes.claim: Widespread discontents with diffuse or hard-to-name causes (inequality, debt, lost status) tend to attach themselves to large, visible institutions that did not cause them, because a salient target is easier to mobilize against than an abstract structural problem.

nodes.title: Diffuse Individually-Minor Harms Sum to a Massive Aggregate
nodes.claim: A harm that is small for any one person can be one of the largest burdens in the world once multiplied across a population of billions.

nodes.title: Director Discretion Beats Peer Panels at Backing Unconventional Talent
nodes.claim: Giving an empowered director discretion to back people and ideas directly, and judging success across a whole portfolio, surfaces unconventional talent that peer-panel review filters out.

nodes.title: Disinvestment Traps a Place in a Downward Spiral
nodes.claim: Excluding higher-income residents and capital from an area produces disinvestment - a collapsing tax base, thinning amenities, and rising insecurity - which harms the remaining poor more than an inflow would.

nodes.title: Displacing an Externality Creates New, Concentrated Opponents
nodes.claim: A charge that pushes an externality onto bypass routes rather than eliminating it mobilises fresh, geographically concentrated opposition, even as it lowers aggregate harm.

nodes.title: Distributed Supply Without Shared Visibility Strands Inventory
nodes.claim: When a scarce good is allocated through several parallel supply chains whose participants cannot see each other's true inventory, demand cannot locate supply, so goods sit unused amid overwhelming demand - a coordination failure distinct from genuine scarcity.

nodes.title: Distribution Shift Degrades a Model Trained on Narrow Data
nodes.claim: A statistical model trained on data from one setting degrades when applied to another, because differences the training data never captured shift the input distribution the model relies on.

nodes.title: Division of Labor Scales Scientific Production
nodes.claim: Treating research as a production output built by teams of specialists — theorists, statisticians, programmers, code-checkers, Red Teams, writers — rather than by all-rounder lone scientists, raises both the quality and the quantity of science, the same way the division of labor raises productivity generally.

nodes.title: Domestic Co-Benefits Make Transboundary Cooperation Self-Interested
nodes.claim: International environmental agreements succeed when each signatory captures most of the benefit of its own compliance at home. Where abatement is domestically profitable, the treaty ratifies a self-interested action rather than compelling an altruistic one — and where it is not, no treaty design substitutes for the missing incentive.

nodes.title: Dramatic Events Crowd Out Consequential Ones in Attention
nodes.claim: Attention is drawn to vivid, dramatic (often violent) events rather than to the diffuse, gradual changes that actually have the largest downstream effects, biasing perceived importance toward spectacle over consequence.

nodes.title: Drop-In Substitutes Diffuse Faster Than Architectural Replacements
nodes.claim: Of two innovations offering comparable benefits, the one that swaps a component inside an unchanged system will be adopted far more widely and quickly than the one that changes the system's architecture — because adoption cost scales with how much surrounding practice, tooling, regulation, and expertise must be discarded, not with the size of the benefit offered.

nodes.title: Drudgery Is Allocated by Power
nodes.claim: The burden of necessary but degrading toil is distributed according to power: the least powerful members of a society — slaves, women, children — are assigned the unchosen, exhausting, low-status labor that everyone depends on but no one with options will do.

nodes.title: Dual-Use Dilemma: Defense Tech Enables Offense
nodes.claim: Technology built to defend against a threat often equally enables causing it. Developing the capability can therefore create a new risk that may exceed the natural one it was meant to address — a reason to be cautious about pre-building defenses for rare hazards.

nodes.title: Durability Claims Cannot Be Validated Faster Than the Asset's Lifetime
nodes.claim: When a technology's central advantage is that it lasts longer, that advantage is unverifiable until roughly as much time has passed as the claimed lifetime — so the evidence needed to justify adoption cannot exist at the moment of adoption, and the decision must rest on accelerated tests, analogy, or trust instead.

nodes.title: Each Increment of Urban Build-Out Raises the Political Cost of the Next
nodes.claim: Development is self-limiting: every unit built adds residents who bear the local cost of the next unit and gain nothing from it, so the political price of each further increment rises. A system that builds freely today mechanically manufactures the constituency that will stop it tomorrow.

nodes.title: Economies of Scale Make Unit Cost a Function of Throughput
nodes.claim: In production subject to strong scale economies, high per-unit costs reflect low volume rather than any inherent floor, so expanding throughput can collapse marginal cost.

nodes.title: Editing Capability Outruns Knowledge of What to Edit
nodes.claim: When a general-purpose intervention tool improves much faster than the domain knowledge required to aim it, the binding constraint on progress silently moves from capability to targeting: practitioners can make almost any change they like and still cannot say which change would help.

nodes.title: Effective Prizes Fill Gaps Left by Existing Incentives, Not Duplicate Them
nodes.claim: Prizes have the most impact when they target problems that patents, markets, or academic funding structurally fail to reward — non-patentable techniques, insufficiently profitable-but-valuable inventions, or research nobody has a commercial incentive to conduct — rather than competing head-on with incentives that already exist.

nodes.title: Effective Treatments Can Outrun Mechanistic Understanding
nodes.claim: A therapy can be robustly and repeatedly shown to work while its actual causal pathway remains unknown, decoupling clinical adoption from explanation.

nodes.title: Efficient Function Often Produces Beauty as a Byproduct
nodes.claim: Optimising hard for a practical end frequently yields beauty as a side effect, but utility is only one route to beauty, not the only one.

nodes.title: Egalitarian Leveling Suppresses Domineering Individuals
nodes.claim: Egalitarian groups collectively punish or execute would-be bullies, a reverse-dominance mechanism that curbs domination without formal institutions.

nodes.title: Electoral Accountability Can Substitute for Public Consultation
nodes.claim: A clear electoral mandate to build can substitute for open-ended consultation, treating the election result rather than a vocal minority at hearings as the democratic authorisation.

nodes.title: Elite Anti-Consumption Signals Status
nodes.claim: Much environmental moralizing functions as elite status-differentiation rather than impact-minimization: once mass consumption becomes universal, elites distinguish themselves by disdaining it, moralizing selectively about low-impact behaviors while ignoring their own high-impact ones.

nodes.title: Elite Capture in Semi-Autonomous Institutions
nodes.claim: The process by which governance authority in semi-autonomous or special jurisdictions is captured by a small, organized elite - developers, investors, political sponsors - redirecting state capacity toward rent extraction rather than broad public goods.

nodes.title: Elite Overproduction Destabilizes States
nodes.claim: When the number of elite aspirants exceeds the available elite positions, intra-elite competition intensifies, factional conflict rises, cooperative norms erode and institutions become politicized - reducing the state's ability to act coherently, particularly under crisis.

nodes.title: Elite Taste Propagates Downward Through Prestige Channels
nodes.claim: Fashions adopted by high-status commissioners - governments, corporations, elite architects - diffuse downward and reshape norms, while lower-status buyers insulated from those channels retain older preferences longer.

nodes.title: Embedded Evaluation Outperforms Outside Study
nodes.claim: Studying a system by partnering with the organizations that run it - rather than from an external vantage - yields access to otherwise-hidden data and to variation that can be exploited for causal inference, and surfaces the questions actually worth asking.

nodes.title: Enabling Technology Gates Policy Adoption
nodes.claim: A sound policy can stay infeasible until a complementary technology matures, because without it the policy's own mechanism produces intolerable side effects.

nodes.title: Encoding Expert Tacit Knowledge Into the Product Removes the Skill Barrier
nodes.claim: Embedding an expert's hard-won judgment directly into a device or its consumable inputs lets non-experts reproduce expert results without acquiring the underlying skill, collapsing training cost and making quality portable.

nodes.title: Energy Cost Is an Upstream Constraint on Almost Everything Else
nodes.claim: The price of energy is an input to health, food, water, transport, materials, and information, so a change in it propagates into nearly every other outcome. Energy policy is therefore not a sector policy but a multiplier on general welfare, and expensive energy is a diffuse, continuous cost rather than a contained one.

nodes.title: Enforcement Creates a Self-Reinforcing Norm Cascade
nodes.claim: Sanctioning a behaviour makes it rarer, rarity makes it more deviant, deviance raises the moral cost of doing it, and the higher moral cost drives it rarer still - a virtuous cycle enforcement alone could not achieve.

nodes.title: Engineering Reversibility and Locality Enables Consent to Irreversible Deployment
nodes.claim: Redesigning a self-spreading intervention so that it decays after a set number of generations or stays confined to a local population converts an unaccountable global act into a testable, opt-in one that neighbours can consent to.

nodes.title: Environmental Toxins Carry Large Hidden Behavioral Costs
nodes.claim: Environmental toxins can impose enormous, society-wide costs through diffuse, delayed, and invisible channels — lowered cognition, worse health, and increased crime — that are easy to overlook precisely because no single victim or event is dramatic.

nodes.title: Epidemics Expose Latent Institutional Weakness
nodes.claim: Crises reveal pre-existing structural weaknesses in state institutions rather than creating them. Failure under a pandemic is a readout of accumulated sclerosis, misallocation and politicization that was already present and untested.

nodes.title: Equal Proportional Gains Defuse Distributional Conflict
nodes.claim: Giving every affected owner the same percentage uplift from a redevelopment removes the fights over who wins more that sink schemes relying on case-by-case compensation.

nodes.title: Equalizing Local Revenue Destroys the Local Incentive to Host
nodes.claim: When revenue raised locally from a facility or development is redistributed away from the community that hosts it, that community keeps the disamenity and loses the compensation. Hosting becomes a pure cost, and the community stops agreeing to it.

nodes.title: Escalating Weapon Lethality Forces New De-Escalation Conventions
nodes.claim: When technological change raises a conflict-resolution ritual's potential lethality (from clubs and spears to dueling pistols), participants develop new face-saving conventions — such as deliberately firing into the air — that preserve the ritual's reconciliation function while reducing its body count.

nodes.title: Escaping a Jurisdiction Escapes Its Regulatory Costs
nodes.claim: A mobile activity can relocate beyond a jurisdiction's reach to shed the labour, tax, and land rules that bind its land-based competitors, revealing how much of cost is regulation.

nodes.title: Evaluate a Good by the Experience of Its Actual Users, Not Its Connoisseurs
nodes.claim: A thing should be judged by the experience of the people who actually live with and use it, not by the connoisseurs who theorise about it.

nodes.title: Every Fix Adds Complexity That Breeds the Next Problem
nodes.claim: Each fix applied to a complex system adds oversight, rules, and interacting parts, which generate new problems requiring further fixes — a one-way ratchet toward ever greater complexity and worse outcomes.

nodes.title: Evolutionary Function as a Basis for Defining Dysfunction
nodes.claim: Evolutionary history provides the only non-arbitrary biological basis for distinguishing functional traits from dysfunctions. A trait's function is the effect it was selected for, so dysfunction means the failure of an evolved system rather than social undesirability.

nodes.title: Excluding a Stakeholder From the Decision Externalizes Costs Onto Them
nodes.claim: When a decision is confined to one group, the uncompensated costs fall on the excluded parties, who have no vote and no recourse.

nodes.title: Excluding Volatile Components Trades Coverage for a Cleaner Signal
nodes.claim: Stripping high-variance items from a series produces a smoother, more forecast-relevant measure, but by construction omits prices people actually pay, so the choice of what to exclude is contestable and can be read as motivated.

nodes.title: Exhaustive Empirical Search Substitutes for Absent Theory
nodes.claim: Where theory cannot narrow the candidate set, systematic brute-force search over that set can still find the answer — provided each trial is cheap and fast enough that the search space can be covered. Search buys knowledge with iterations instead of with understanding.

nodes.title: Existential Risk Follows an Inverted-U (Time of Perils)
nodes.claim: Over the course of development, existential risk rises and then falls — an inverted-U. A poor society spends almost everything on consumption (so risk climbs as technology advances), but as it gets rich enough to value life highly, it shifts resources to safety and risk begins to fall, eventually toward zero.

nodes.title: Expected Unreliability Suppresses Long-Run Capital Investment
nodes.claim: Beyond the direct cost of outages, the expectation that an input will be unavailable when needed causes firms to permanently reorganize around lower productivity — choosing less capital-intensive, more traditional, more redundant methods — so the largest damage from unreliability is the investment that is never made rather than the output lost during any particular failure.

nodes.title: Experiment Cycle Time Bounds the Rate of Discovery
nodes.claim: The speed at which a field learns is set by how long one iteration of its basic experiment takes, not by how clever its practitioners or how powerful its tools are. Where the organism, material, or process under study imposes a long cycle, the field is rate-limited by that clock regardless of how much money or talent is applied.

nodes.title: Expertise Breeds Fixation on Familiar Solutions
nodes.claim: Deep expertise can make people fixate on familiar approaches and overlook better ones, so accumulated knowledge becomes a blinker as well as a tool.

nodes.title: Expertise Can Disqualify Rather Than Qualify an Aesthetic Judgment
nodes.claim: Specialist training can systematically diverge a judge's experience from how most stakeholders experience a thing, making experts worse, not better, at deciding what to build for the public.

nodes.title: Explanatory Models Shape Stigma and Treatment
nodes.claim: How a condition is explained causally affects stigma, hope, and treatment behavior.

nodes.title: Explicitly Tying Disruption to Its Payoff Buys Public Tolerance
nodes.claim: People will accept sharper short-term disruption when it is explicitly framed as the price of a faster, lasting benefit.

nodes.title: Exponential Threats Reward Early Detection Disproportionately
nodes.claim: For any process that grows exponentially, the value of acting is front-loaded: shaving time off detection and response early prevents vastly more total harm than the same intervention applied after growth has compounded.

nodes.title: Exposure Pathway Determines Hazard More Than Intrinsic Potency
nodes.claim: The danger a substance or agent poses is a joint function of its intrinsic potency and the route by which it can actually reach the tissue it damages. Where a plausible pathway is absent, extreme potency produces little risk; where a pathway is efficient, modest potency can be lethal. Hazard figures quoted without their assumed route of exposure are therefore not merely imprecise — they can be wrong by many orders of magnitude.

nodes.title: Expropriation Loses Legitimacy as Ownership Fragments
nodes.claim: Compulsory purchase is politically easy only when affected owners are all net beneficiaries of the result; as ownership fragments, expropriation creates concentrated losers and becomes politically unviable.

nodes.title: External Classification Forges an Internal Coalition
nodes.claim: When outsiders lump distinct actors together and treat them as one group, the imposed category can become a real coalition with shared interests and identity.

nodes.title: Extractive Institutions Can Win Wars Yet Foreclose Growth
nodes.claim: Coercive systems that efficiently pull men and taxes from a population can build formidable states in the short run but starve long-run investment and eventually fail against developed rivals.

nodes.title: Extrapolating From High Doses Misstates Low-Dose Risk
nodes.claim: Drawing a straight line from effects measured at extreme doses down to tiny doses can badly misstate low-dose risk, because the biological response need not be linear and repair processes dominate at low exposure.

nodes.title: Falling Input Costs Make Latent Projects Feasible
nodes.claim: A steep, exogenous fall in the cost of a key input can flip a long-infeasible project into an obvious one, without any change in the underlying science or goal — feasibility is a moving threshold set by input prices, not a fixed property of the project.

nodes.title: Falling Ore Grades Are Paid in Energy, Water, and Waste Volume
nodes.claim: Extracting the same quantity of a material from progressively poorer sources requires processing progressively more matter, so the cost migrates out of scarcity and into throughput: more rock moved, more water consumed, more energy spent, and more waste generated per unit of product.

nodes.title: Falling Transaction Costs Restructure Economic Geography
nodes.claim: Sharp reductions in the cost of moving goods, people, or information across distance trigger disproportionate, system-wide reorganizations of trade, settlement, and social life.

nodes.title: Falling Transaction Risk Enables Larger Fixed-Capital Investment
nodes.claim: As the risk of loss in trade falls, larger fixed-capital investments become worthwhile, because the expected return is no longer wiped out by frequent catastrophic loss.

nodes.title: Familiarity Dissolves Glamour
nodes.claim: Once a longed-for technology becomes universal it becomes 'just life' — its benefits are taken for granted and its remaining flaws become the focus of complaint.

nodes.title: Faster Growth Shrinks Cumulative Risk
nodes.claim: Accelerating economic growth raises risk in the short run but lowers the cumulative probability of existential catastrophe, because it brings society to the wealth level where it invests in safety sooner — compressing the dangerous "time of perils" and shrinking the total area under the risk curve.

nodes.title: Fear Transfers From an Associated Technology
nodes.claim: A technology can be crippled by fear and hostility earned by a different but associated technology, as the public transfers dread from the one to the other regardless of their actual relationship.

nodes.title: Fertility Decline Can Precede Economic Development
nodes.claim: The demographic transition is not necessarily caused by economic development: fertility can fall sharply in a society that is still poor, rural, illiterate, and burdened by very high infant mortality, provided the normative constraint on limiting births is relaxed. Culture can be the leading variable and development the lagging one.

nodes.title: Fertility Responds to Incentives Once Childbearing Is Optional
nodes.claim: Once contraception and women's legal/economic autonomy make childbearing a genuine choice, fertility becomes responsive to the private cost-benefit calculus of reproduction — especially the costs that fall on mothers — to a degree that was impossible when childbearing was effectively compulsory.

nodes.title: Filtering: New Supply Lowers Prices Down-Market
nodes.claim: Building new homes — even high-end "luxury" ones — lowers prices and rents across the whole market, including at the bottom, through "filtering": wealthier residents move into the new stock, vacating older units, which increases availability and competition down the income scale.

nodes.title: Financing Structures Must Match an Industry's Capital and Time Profile
nodes.claim: Venture capital suits fast, high-margin, low-capital software and pharma but is mismatched to the long timescales and heavy capital of materials, so the wrong financing structure starves an industry of appropriate funding.

nodes.title: Fiscal and Military Pressure Drives Administrative Quantification
nodes.claim: The cash demands of professional warfare force states to adopt systematic accounting and measurement, raising their capacity to tax, borrow, and administer.

nodes.title: Fiscal Capacity Can Substitute for Political Constraint in Good Governance
nodes.claim: Where rulers are not constrained by a parliament, high fiscal capacity — cheap, sustainable debt — can still secure internal peace and fund productive investment.

nodes.title: Fiscal Self-Interest Turns Governments Into Sponsors of Development
nodes.claim: When a local government's own budget improves as a direct result of a land use, it stops behaving as a regulator of that use and starts behaving as its promoter. Aligning the fiscal accounts converts development from something a council permits into something it actively seeks.

nodes.title: Fixed-Basket Indices Overstate Cost Because Agents Substitute
nodes.claim: When one option's relative price rises, people shift consumption toward cheaper alternatives, so a fixed-weight index - which assumes the old basket - overstates the welfare loss actually borne, and updating the weights corrects part of the bias.

nodes.title: Forced-Sale Thresholds Overcome Holdout Problems in Land Assembly
nodes.claim: Where a valuable transaction requires many owners to agree, unanimity gives every individual a veto and the power to extract the entire surplus, so the deal fails. Replacing unanimity with a supermajority threshold, agreed in advance, lets the group capture gains that no member could have realized alone.

nodes.title: Format Standardization Trades Expressive Range for Access Speed
nodes.claim: Predictable structural conventions constrain stylistic expression but let readers locate relevant information faster - a genuine benefit that reform of writing norms must preserve.

nodes.title: Fragmented Ownership Produces Dysfunctional Urban Form
nodes.claim: Where land is divided into many small plots and public planning is weak, laissez-faire development produces ribbon sprawl, roads that go nowhere, and awkward residual parcels, because owners cannot coordinate on a street network that works for the whole.

nodes.title: Free or Improved Options Reveal Latent Demand
nodes.claim: Offering a free or better option draws in people who were quietly getting by on worse arrangements, so measured take-up overstates the pre-existing acute need.

nodes.title: Free-Riding Ends When Uncompensated Providers Gain Exit Options
nodes.claim: When a positive externality has historically been extracted for free from a provider who couldn't refuse, the free-riding persists only as long as the provider lacks bargaining power; once they gain exit options, provision drops toward the privately optimal (under-)level unless it is now paid for.

nodes.title: Front-Loaded Maintenance Beats Reactive Repair
nodes.claim: Doing maintenance in advance -- anticipating failures and fixing wear the moment it appears -- is far cheaper and safer than waiting for things to break and repairing them reactively, because failures tend to arrive at the worst possible moment.

nodes.title: Front-Loaded Transition Costs With Lagged Benefits Block Welfare-Improving Reform
nodes.claim: A reform whose costs land immediately and whose benefits arrive only after years of investment will be defeated politically even when it is clearly net-positive, because the losers experience a certain loss now while the winners receive an uncertain gain later — and buying out the transition period is therefore the decisive intervention, not further argument about the long-run payoff.

nodes.title: Frontline Ground Truth Beats the Central Record
nodes.claim: The person whose hands are physically on a good, and who can act on it now, holds more reliable and current knowledge than any central record or official policy; systems should be built to extract that frontline knowledge rather than to trust the central model.

nodes.title: Full-Scale Rehearsal Surfaces Integration Failures Before Deployment
nodes.claim: Building a complete working replica of a system at reduced scale, before committing to the real deployment, reveals the failures that arise from interactions between components — failures that no amount of component-level testing will find, because they do not exist at the component level.

nodes.title: General-Purpose Architectures Displace Task-Specific Ones
nodes.claim: Progress shifts from narrow systems hand-built for one task toward single architectures that absorb many tasks, so capability generalizes across domains rather than being re-engineered for each.

nodes.title: General-Purpose Methods Transfer Across Unrelated Domains
nodes.claim: A single underlying technique, once developed for one problem, becomes a template reused across seemingly distinct fields, so activities we treat as unrelated in fact share one logic.

nodes.title: General-Purpose Research Is Undersupplied by Markets
nodes.claim: Research with broad, long-term applicability is systematically undersupplied by decentralized markets, because it is expensive, its applications are uncertain, its benefits spill across sectors, and it cannot easily be patented or turned into a product.

nodes.title: Geometry Can Substitute for Brute Force in Reaching a Physical Frontier
nodes.claim: Redesigning the shape or configuration of a system changes how a fixed input is concentrated, so the same physical target - here extreme pressure - can be met with less raw force, energy, or capital.

nodes.title: Giving Citizens a Stake Starts a Virtuous Cycle of Further Reform
nodes.claim: Distributing rights or property gives newly enfranchised beneficiaries both the means and the motive to lobby for additional reform, compounding institutional improvement over time.

nodes.title: Glamour Requires Concealed Trade-Offs to Function
nodes.claim: An image is alluring precisely because it hides the difficulty, cost, and boredom that come with the real thing; glamour is an illusion that focuses longing by omission.

nodes.title: Goal Misgeneralization Persists Even With Correct Specification
nodes.claim: An agent can learn the right behavior in training yet internalize the wrong goal, so when the deployment environment shifts subtly its capabilities generalize but its objective does not.

nodes.title: Grand Visions Mobilize Support Until Costs Localize, Then Support Collapses
nodes.claim: Sweeping infrastructure or policy visions win broad initial backing because their benefits are abstract, future, and shared by everyone, but that consensus dissolves once concrete plans reveal exactly who bears the disruption, demolition, and cost — supporting a vision in principle and supporting its actual site-specific consequences are two different votes.

nodes.title: Group Non-Violent Norms Create an Opening for Individual Defectors
nodes.claim: When a majority commits to peace, the few willing to use violence face reluctant opposition and can capture outsize gains, so a peaceful norm creates a niche for predators.

nodes.title: Groupthink Suppresses Heterodox Science
nodes.claim: Because individuals take their cues on "what is sensible to believe" from prevailing consensus, scientific institutions systematically suppress findings and theories that contradict the dominant view — hurting both reproducibility (dissonant results get hidden or distorted) and innovation (heterodox lines go unfunded).

nodes.title: Growth Drives the Demographic Transition
nodes.claim: Economic growth and urbanization, not deliberate population control, are what bring fertility down: as societies move from rural agrarian life to urban industrial life, children shift from farm labor to costly long-term investments, so people have fewer of them and invest more in each.

nodes.title: Guaranteed Demand Can Substitute for an Undiscovered Market
nodes.claim: An advance purchase or procurement guarantee gives a manufacturer an initial buyer, letting a material scale down its cost curve until organic applications emerge that the market could not foresee.

nodes.title: Handoffs Between Specialized Roles Are Where Projects Fail
nodes.claim: When discovery and production are done by different people who 'speak different languages,' the transition between them becomes the point where knowledge is lost and projects die.

nodes.title: Hard-to-Measure Outcomes Impede Evidence-Based Reform
nodes.claim: When the outcome you ultimately care about (an increased stock of knowledge, social welfare) is hard to define and measure, you cannot cleanly compare policies — which pushes evaluators toward ever-more-elaborate econometrics and stalls evidence-based reform. The response is humility and proxy/retrospective evaluation, not giving up.

nodes.title: Hazard Lethality Tracks Wealth, Not Hazard Intensity
nodes.claim: The lethality of an environmental hazard is determined less by its intrinsic danger than by the wealth-dependent infrastructure available to mitigate it.

nodes.title: Hedging Demand Concentrates on Financial Outcomes, Not the Events Behind Them
nodes.claim: People hedge the market prices that events affect rather than the events themselves, because hedging the financial outcome implicitly covers all of its underlying causes at once.

nodes.title: Heed Market Price Signals Over Intuitions of Calamity
nodes.claim: When market prices (e.g. very low bond yields) and one's intuition of impending calamity disagree, the price signal — which aggregates the views and money of many participants — usually deserves more weight than the intuition.

nodes.title: Hidden Domestic Labor Is Economically Invisible
nodes.claim: A vast amount of human labor — the unpaid processing and reproductive work of turning raw inputs into usable food and running a household — is economically invisible (uncounted in market statistics) yet consumes an enormous share of human time and capacity, especially women's.

nodes.title: Hierarchy Lets Leaders Externalize the Costs of Conflict
nodes.claim: Hierarchy lets leaders capture the spoils of aggression while making followers bear the fighting risk, shifting incentives toward more frequent conflict.

nodes.title: High Background Churn Masks Marginal Treatment Effects
nodes.claim: When baseline turnover is already high, a policy-driven increment in movement is statistically small and easily mistaken for no effect, so studies can miss real but marginal displacement.

nodes.title: High Land Prices Push Logistics Off-Site
nodes.claim: When on-site space is extremely valuable, activities that consume floor space — storage, fuel handling, production — are pushed off-site to a central facility on cheaper land.

nodes.title: High Margins Remove the Pressure to Cut Costs
nodes.claim: When a product sells at a price far above its cost of goods, there is little pressure to reduce that cost, so obvious efficiencies go unrealised and the price stays decoupled from the cost of production.

nodes.title: High-Survival Samples Test for Survivorship Bias
nodes.claim: To test whether an observed pattern is an artifact of survivorship bias, find sub-populations that survived at near-complete rates (for reasons unrelated to the trait in question) and check whether the pattern still holds; if it does, selective attrition cannot be the main cause.

nodes.title: Higher-Tier Government Approval Is a Choke Point on Local Reform
nodes.claim: A local policy that touches state- or federally-controlled assets can be stalled indefinitely by the higher authority's permission requirement, giving distant actors a veto over local choices.

nodes.title: Hopelessness, Not Hardship, Drives Suicide
nodes.claim: The lethal ingredient in suicidal depression may be hopelessness — the sense that suffering is permanent and nothing can change — rather than the severity of hardship itself. A crisis that supplies an end-in-sight, novelty, or urgent purpose can lower suicidality even while raising distress.

nodes.title: Housing Restrictions Misallocate Labor and Reduce Growth
nodes.claim: When the most productive cities restrict housing supply, workers are priced out of the places where they would be most productive, forcing a spatial misallocation of labor that lowers aggregate output and growth — not merely local unaffordability.

nodes.title: Housing Shortage Is an Upstream Meta-Cause
nodes.claim: A housing shortage in productive areas is an upstream cause whose effects propagate into many seemingly unrelated problems — low productivity, inequality, regional divergence, low fertility, obesity, carbon emissions, financial instability — because housing determines the location and supply of people, the most important economic input.

nodes.title: Housing Shortages Are Regulatory, Not Natural
nodes.claim: Persistent housing shortages in productive cities are caused by regulatory restrictions on building, not by intrinsic scarcity of land or high construction costs. The diagnostic is the ratio of a home's market price to its production cost: when price far exceeds cost, the gap measures the "regulatory tax" of permission to build.

nodes.title: How a Metric Is Constructed Changes the Conclusions Drawn From It
nodes.claim: The methodological choices embedded in an index - base period, weighting, coverage, formula - systematically bias its output, so two defensible constructions of 'the same' quantity yield materially different numbers and support different conclusions.

nodes.title: Humans Defer Excessively to Assistive Automation
nodes.claim: People paired with an assistive automated tool tend to defer to it more than they should, so the human-plus-machine combination can perform worse than either the machine's benchmark or an unaided human in some respects.

nodes.title: Implementation Lag Gives Opponents Time to Regroup
nodes.claim: Reforms that depend on slow implementation let a recalcitrant actor stall in hope that the next government reverses the rule, converting delay into repeal.

nodes.title: Imported State Capacity
nodes.claim: Borrowing an external institution wholesale - a foreign court, a foreign standard, a foreign regulator - to substitute for domestic capacity that does not yet exist, buying immediate credibility while the domestic version is built.

nodes.title: Importing a Method From a Distant Field Cracks a Stuck Problem
nodes.claim: A problem that resists a field's own tools often yields to a method imported from a distant discipline, so the further a solver's expertise is from the problem, the better the odds of a fresh, decisive approach.

nodes.title: Improving Substitute Technology Erodes an Incumbent's Cost Advantage
nodes.claim: Steady performance gains in a competing method shrink the incumbent's price edge until the choice flips.

nodes.title: Improving the Housing Stock Destroys Naturally-Occurring Affordable Housing
nodes.claim: Any program that upgrades old buildings necessarily removes the cheap, low-quality homes whose low price came precisely from their poor condition.

nodes.title: Incentives Accelerate Peer Review Without Degrading Quality
nodes.claim: Modest incentives -- cash rewards, shorter deadlines, public disclosure of turnaround times -- reliably speed up peer review, and (contrary to worry) do so without measurably lowering review quality.

nodes.title: Incremental Sensible Steps Compound into Lock-In
nodes.claim: A large, hard-to-reverse regime can emerge without anyone ever deciding on it, when each individual step is a locally sensible adjustment; the accumulation locks in an outcome that no one would have chosen as a whole.

nodes.title: Incumbent Capitalization Blocks Reform
nodes.claim: Reform is hardest where the status quo is already "capitalized" into asset prices: homeowners who paid prices far above construction cost would lose wealth if building were liberalized, so they form an organized bloc against reform — and the more harmful the restriction, the larger their stake in keeping it.

nodes.title: Incumbent Cost Estimates of Compliance Are Systematically Inflated
nodes.claim: Firms asked to estimate what a proposed regulation would cost them reliably report figures well above what compliance actually costs, and those figures fall sharply once the estimate is scrutinized or the rule is imposed. The estimate is a negotiating position produced by an interested party, not a measurement.

nodes.title: Incumbent Experts Resist Devaluing the Past
nodes.claim: Experts who have invested heavily in mastering a field's history have a vested interest in maintaining that the past is supreme, because progress that supersedes the old canon would devalue their accumulated knowledge and status. This biases authoritative opinion toward pessimism and reverence.

nodes.title: Incumbent Gatekeepers Suppress Challenges to the Dominant Paradigm
nodes.claim: When senior insiders control funding, publishing, and hiring, they filter out work that challenges the dominant paradigm or crosses disciplinary lines, suppressing the very ideas most likely to overturn a stuck field.

nodes.title: Incumbent Infrastructure Preempts New Products Where Real Demand Exists
nodes.claim: When demand to hedge or trade a risk is genuine, existing institutions have already built a product to serve it, so the absence of a new product is itself evidence that the demand is absent.

nodes.title: Independent Errors Cancel in Aggregate Estimates
nodes.claim: Averaging many independently formed guesses yields an estimate more accurate than nearly any individual guess, because errors that are uncorrelated across judges cancel out in the mean. Accuracy comes from the independence of the judgments, not from the expertise of the judges — a crowd of mostly ignorant people can outperform the experts inside it.

nodes.title: Indexing a Payment to a Metric Politicizes Its Measurement
nodes.claim: Once benefits, wages, or taxes are automatically tied to a statistic, every party affected acquires a direct financial stake in how that statistic is computed, turning a technocratic measurement into a lobbying battleground.

nodes.title: Individual Boycotts Rarely Drive Systemic Change
nodes.claim: Large-scale moral progress has historically not been achieved through individual consumer boycotts.

nodes.title: Industrializing a Biological Process Requires Hijacking a Living Host
nodes.claim: A molecule too complex to synthesize chemically can only be made at scale by redirecting the machinery of a living host to produce it, so industrialization means engineering an organism rather than a reaction.

nodes.title: Industry-Funded Science Manufactures Doubt
nodes.claim: Incumbents who profit from a harmful product can sponsor research and experts to contest the evidence of harm, manufacturing enough apparent scientific uncertainty to delay regulation.

nodes.title: Inferring a Hidden Cause From Observed Outcomes
nodes.claim: An unobservable underlying quality can be estimated by measuring the observable outcomes it produces across many cases.

nodes.title: Informal Non-Market Buffers Absorb Shocks the Formal Market Cannot Price
nodes.claim: Most people at risk of destitution stay housed through non-market, relational arrangements — a relative's spare room traded for chores and affection — that no formal market prices or measures.

nodes.title: Information Asymmetry Creates a Market for Lemons
nodes.claim: When buyers cannot verify quality before purchase, low-quality products drive out high-quality ones, collapsing trust and depressing demand for the whole category.

nodes.title: Infrastructure Capacity, Not Permission, Is the Ultimate Constraint on Growth
nodes.claim: Permission to build is necessary but not sufficient. Where water, sewerage, roads or schools are already at capacity, upzoning delivers nothing, and a jurisdiction that wants to prevent growth can do so simply by declining to expand the infrastructure - a veto that leaves no zoning fingerprints at all.

nodes.title: Infrastructure Cost Variation Reflects Institutions, Not Geography
nodes.claim: The cost of building comparable infrastructure varies enormously across countries, and that variation tracks a country's general construction costs rather than the physical features of individual projects — implying regulation and procurement, not geology, drive the difference.

nodes.title: Infrastructure Outlives the Coalition That Built It
nodes.claim: A coalition's durable legacy is often the infrastructure it built — safe routes, larger shipping, commercial law — which persists long after the coalition's own power fades.

nodes.title: Infrastructure Persists Once Embedded Despite Superior Alternatives
nodes.claim: A working, amortised, deeply embedded network can persist for a century after a more efficient alternative emerges, because ripping it out costs more than tolerating its inefficiency.

nodes.title: Innovation Concentrates in the Largest Market
nodes.claim: Technological innovation gravitates to the largest and most profitable market, because that is where the returns to new methods are greatest; economies outside that market are then stranded with best-practice techniques designed for someone else's factor prices and scale.

nodes.title: Innovation Requires Spillover Capture
nodes.claim: Sustained investment in innovation requires institutions that can capture a sufficient share of the value they create. Where spillovers are fast and complete, private incentives to invest collapse, however large the social return.

nodes.title: Innovations Must Beat the Incumbent on Every Dimension, Not on Net
nodes.claim: Where the decision-maker bears a large, public downside from failure but captures little of the upside from success, an innovation is not adopted for being better on net; it must dominate the incumbent on every dimension the incumbent is already good at, because any single regression becomes the story told about the decision.

nodes.title: Input Availability, Not Lost Knowledge, Can Gate Quality
nodes.claim: When a product's quality depends on a specific input, the good can degrade or vanish even while the know-how survives, because the binding constraint is access to the ingredient rather than the recipe.

nodes.title: Insecure or Undefined Property Rights Suppress Investment
nodes.claim: When it is unclear who owns a resource, or when ownership can be reallocated, potential developers cannot be sure of capturing returns and therefore decline to invest.

nodes.title: Institutional Adoption Cascades via Normalization
nodes.claim: Adoption of a contested asset or technology by credible institutions is self-reinforcing: each adopter lowers the perceived risk and stigma for the next, so adoption cascades once a threshold of reputable players is crossed.

nodes.title: Institutional Form Shapes the Direction of Progress
nodes.claim: Different institutional arrangements systematically favor different kinds of innovation. Startups favor speed and focus, universities favor prestige and specialization, large integrated labs favor breadth and long horizons - and no single form dominates across all innovation types.

nodes.title: Institutional Reluctance to Admit Uncertainty Blocks Experimentation
nodes.claim: Institutions resist experimenting (randomizing, piloting, using lotteries) because doing so would publicly admit they don't already know the right answer — a status and legitimacy cost that outweighs, for them, the value of the knowledge an experiment would produce.

nodes.title: Institutional Sclerosis Reduces Crisis Responsiveness
nodes.claim: Accumulated rent-seeking and bureaucratic rigidity reduce a state's ability to respond rapidly to novel threats. Over time interest groups entrench privileges, regulatory systems thicken, and administrative attention shifts toward internal maintenance - which raises friction exactly where speed matters.

nodes.title: Institutional Sclerosis
nodes.claim: The accumulation of outdated, rent-seeking or inefficient policies that are politically easy to introduce and extremely hard to repeal, so that the stock of bad rules grows monotonically and the aggregate drag compounds.

nodes.title: Institutions Cannot Be Copied Ahead of the Process That Produces Them
nodes.claim: The institutions of a capable state are the residue of a long sequence of bargains, not a template that can be adopted directly. Importing the forms without the underlying process produces institutions that exist on paper and do not function, because the conditions that made them enforceable were never built.

nodes.title: Institutions Diffuse Because They Confer Competitive Advantage
nodes.claim: In a competitive system, institutional innovations spread not only by conquest but by imitation, because adopting them improves a unit's ability to compete.

nodes.title: Instrumentation Drives Scientific Discovery
nodes.claim: Major scientific discoveries are frequently driven by new or improved instruments rather than by new theory: each advance in observational capability opens a window in which the unexpected is found, often serendipitously and far from the instrument's intended purpose.

nodes.title: Intangible Capital Drives Progress
nodes.claim: Much technological progress is intangible: improvements in ideas, recipes, techniques, software, and know-how raise output and quality even when the visible physical tools are unchanged. Because it can't be touched, this capital is systematically underrated.

nodes.title: Integrating Discovery and Invention Accelerates Progress
nodes.claim: Bringing scientific discovery and practical invention under the same roof, project, and people accelerates progress, because it lets the reciprocal feedback between theory and engineering run without the friction of organizational handoffs.

nodes.title: Interconnection and Fluid Affiliation Lower Inter-Group Violence
nodes.claim: Trade, intermarriage, and shared culture give groups a stake in peace, lowering inter-group violence, while self-sufficient isolation removes those brakes.

nodes.title: Interconnection Delay Strands Completed Generation Capacity
nodes.claim: A finished generating asset delivers no value until it is connected to transmission, so interconnection queues can neutralize an otherwise-complete project for years.

nodes.title: Interdisciplinary Work Is Penalized Early and Rewarded Late
nodes.claim: Work that crosses disciplines is funded less, reviewed more slowly, and cited later than specialised work, yet when it lands it tends to have larger long-run impact — so short-term incentives penalise exactly the work with the biggest eventual payoff.

nodes.title: Intermittency Caps a Power Source's Value Independent of Its Cost
nodes.claim: Energy that is available only when conditions permit cannot by itself meet continuous demand, so its usefulness is bounded by intermittency no matter how cheap it becomes.

nodes.title: Invasiveness Trades Off Against Signal Fidelity
nodes.claim: A measurement system faces a trade-off between how invasive it is and how faithful a signal it captures: non-invasive sensors read a blurred signal through intervening material, while implanted ones read a clean signal at the cost of surgical risk.

nodes.title: Invisible Harms Are Systematically Under-Addressed
nodes.claim: A hazard that produces no immediate, visible symptom fails to mobilise the parents, governments, and markets that would act against a visible one, so it persists even when cheap to fix and enormously damaging in aggregate.

nodes.title: Irreversibility of Downstream Errors Sets an Intervention's Risk Tolerance
nodes.claim: How much risk an intervention may run depends on whether its errors are discarded harmlessly or propagate irreversibly into a person or system.

nodes.title: Judging Impact by Attribute Rather Than End-to-End Effect Misleads
nodes.claim: Evaluating something by an intrinsic label instead of its net effect in context produces wrong verdicts, because harms and benefits depend on the whole application, not the material in isolation.

nodes.title: Labor Mobility Diffuses Innovation
nodes.claim: When skilled workers can move freely between firms, the tacit knowledge and best practices they carry diffuse rapidly across a region, raising the innovative output of the cluster as a whole — even though any individual firm losing the worker bears a private cost.

nodes.title: Labor-Intensive Quality Fails When Customers Won't Pay Its Time Cost
nodes.claim: A high-quality method whose cost is dominated by skilled labour time becomes commercially unviable when buyers will not pay a price proportional to that time, regardless of how good the output is.

nodes.title: Labor-Saving Technology Reallocates Human Time
nodes.claim: Technologies that collapse the time cost of a necessary task free up human time and capacity for other ends; successive innovations can reduce the labor a society must devote to a chore by orders of magnitude, with large knock-on effects on who can do what.

nodes.title: Laboratory Performance Does Not Survive the Move to Mass Production
nodes.claim: A result achieved under laboratory conditions degrades sharply when the same artefact is made at volume, because manufacturing introduces variance, cost limits, and unskilled labour that the laboratory suppressed. Closing that gap is a separate engineering problem of comparable difficulty to the original invention.

nodes.title: Land Captures the Gains from Progress
nodes.claim: When housing supply is fixed, improvements in incomes or local amenities are partly captured by landowners as higher prices, rather than benefiting the people who earned the income or use the amenity. Progress turns into land rent.

nodes.title: Land Reform Unlocks a Stable Industrial Labor Supply
nodes.claim: Making rural exit possible converts a seasonally-returning peasant workforce into permanent urban labor, stabilizing industrial production.

nodes.title: Large Organizations Enable Multidisciplinary Discovery
nodes.claim: Large, stable organizations enable forms of innovation that require sustained, cross-disciplinary collaboration — work that markets and startups struggle to fund or coordinate in advance.

nodes.title: Latitude and Climate Interact With a Rule to Produce Geographic Variation
nodes.claim: A uniform rule can produce systematic geographic variation when it interacts with a physical gradient like latitude or climate.

nodes.title: Legitimacy Enables Taxation and Policy Change
nodes.claim: States can only impose costly policies when they possess sufficient legitimacy among key power holders.

nodes.title: Lethality Not Aggression Drives a Species' Violent Death Rate
nodes.claim: A species' violent-death rate can be high even when its members rarely start fights, if its conflicts are unusually lethal when they do occur.

nodes.title: Liberty–Health Tradeoff Is Conditional
nodes.claim: The apparent trade-off between individual liberty and public health is not fixed: it depends on state effectiveness and social coordination. A capable state can protect health with narrower restrictions, so liberty is constrained by state weakness as much as by state power.

nodes.title: Liquidity Requires Participants Who Are Not Trying to Beat the Market
nodes.claim: Efficient, accurate prices emerge only when inelastic non-expert money - savers hedging, gamblers seeking fun - floods a market and creates a surplus that informed traders compete to capture.

nodes.title: Litigation Risk Drives Defensive Over-Documentation
nodes.claim: Where an administrative approval can be overturned in court on procedural grounds, applicants and regulators generate documentation far beyond what any decision-maker will read — not to inform the decision, but to foreclose grounds for challenge. The volume of paperwork tracks the legal attack surface, not the complexity or riskiness of the project.

nodes.title: Local Control Without Local Benefit Produces Undersupply
nodes.claim: When local governments hold the power to block development but capture none of the fiscal or personal gains from it, they systematically restrict housing.

nodes.title: Long-Lived Infrastructure Cost-Recovery Windows Dictate Transition Timing
nodes.claim: Utilities and similar infrastructure providers recover capital costs over multi-decade rate bases (often 50+ years); because new infrastructure must be substantially paid off before being decommissioned without stranding costs on remaining customers, the window for starting a low-carbon transition without an expensive scramble or price shock closes decades before the ultimate deadline.

nodes.title: Losing a Faction Frees a Party to Adopt Its Former Blockers' Agenda
nodes.claim: When an internal faction defects from a party, the remaining members are freed to adopt an agenda that faction had blocked, for good or ill.

nodes.title: Loss-Making Provision Inverts the Incentive to Serve Customers
nodes.claim: When a provider loses money on every unit it sells, its incentives invert: each additional customer, connection, and hour of service is a liability rather than an asset, so the provider rationally works to supply less, not more — and no amount of exhortation to expand coverage will overcome the arithmetic.

nodes.title: Lost Tacit Knowledge Can Erase a Technology
nodes.claim: A working technology can disappear entirely when the tacit know-how and the demand that sustained it are both severed, leaving no one able to reproduce it.

nodes.title: Low Enough Cost Dissolves the Need for Global Coordination
nodes.claim: Free-riding is only worth doing when the action is expensive. Drive the unit cost of a public good low enough and a subset of willing payers can simply provide it alone, which makes the bargaining problem irrelevant rather than solving it.

nodes.title: Low-Tech Manual Methods Beat Grand IT Integration Under Time Pressure
nodes.claim: A cheap, immediately deployable manual method can beat waiting for comprehensive system integration, because integration requires every actor to agree on formats and protocols while the manual method works today and improves incrementally.

nodes.title: Lowering Standards for Speed Degrades Research Quality
nodes.claim: Speeding up science by simply lowering the bar — fast-tracking review, relaxing scrutiny "because the situation is urgent" — degrades quality, in contrast to speed gained from structural transparency reforms. Urgency is not a license to dial down skepticism ("pandemic research exceptionalism").

nodes.title: Lowering the Cost of a Task Multiplies Demand for It
nodes.claim: When a task becomes faster or cheaper, people do much more of it, so total work can rise even as the cost per unit falls — the Jevons paradox applied to labour and services.

nodes.title: Lowering the Cost of an Activity Can Outweigh the Income Effect That Suppresses It
nodes.claim: Where rising incomes reliably reduce an activity - because prosperity raises the opportunity cost of the time it consumes - a large enough fall in the activity's direct cost can reverse the trend for as long as the fall continues. The apparent iron law is a net effect of two forces, and the weaker one can temporarily dominate.

nodes.title: Lowering the Price of a Complement Expands Access to the Primary Good
nodes.claim: Making one good cheaper can expand access to a related good for people who never buy the first good directly, by enlarging the slack that others share with them.

nodes.title: Luxury Status Is Self-Defeating Under Supply Response
nodes.claim: A good prized for its scarcity generates the very high prices that draw entrepreneurs to supply it cheaply, eventually dissolving the prestige that motivated the effort.

nodes.title: Machine Search Can Surface Non-Obvious Recombinations
nodes.claim: Machine systems can scan the entire literature to propose plausible concept pairings that no single human would reach, accelerating cross-field recombination.

nodes.title: Made-to-Order Production Trades Throughput for Variety
nodes.claim: Serving many low-volume variants requires producing each unit on demand, which sharply lowers throughput compared with batch production - so the flexibility to offer variety is bought with a per-unit time cost.

nodes.title: Marginal Precision Has Diminishing and Often Unactionable Value
nodes.claim: Decision-makers usually act the same whether an estimate is 60% or 75%, so paying to sharpen a probability rarely justifies its cost.

nodes.title: Market Efficiency Emerges Only When Correcting Prices Is Profitable
nodes.claim: Prices move toward accuracy only where the market is large enough that a small edge yields real money, because otherwise no expert will spend the effort to correct a mispricing.

nodes.title: Markets for Ideas Favor Modular Innovation
nodes.claim: Markets for ideas reward innovations that are separable, legible and contractible. Ideas that can be patented, demonstrated and sold independently get produced; system-level innovations requiring coordination, integration and tacit knowledge are disadvantaged.

nodes.title: Matching Mechanisms Multiply the Usable Value of Existing Willingness
nodes.claim: Clearing-house exchange chains let would-be contributors who are individually blocked (by incompatibility) still contribute, extracting more usable output from the same pool of willingness.

nodes.title: Material Fire-Classification Codes Set Height Ceilings
nodes.claim: Fire codes that cap the height of cheaper construction materials force buildings to grow wider rather than taller, reshaping the whole urban form.

nodes.title: Mature Fields Advance by Recombination, Not New Primitives
nodes.claim: After a foundational breakthrough, most progress comes from cheaper, lighter, easier-to-process variants and novel combinations of existing elements rather than from inventing entirely new substances, so expecting heroic novelty misreads where value is created.

nodes.title: Mature Systems Fail Predictably; Novel Systems Fail in Unknown Ways
nodes.claim: Established, well-understood technologies break in familiar, anticipated ways, so their failures can be prepared for; novel technologies fail in unexpected ways that no accumulated experience has mapped, making their risks harder to insure against.

nodes.title: Measured Performance Beats Observable Proxies for Selection
nodes.claim: Selecting on directly measured output outperforms selecting on visible proxies like appearance or pedigree, which correlate only loosely with the trait that matters.

nodes.title: Measurement Cost Determines Which Subjects Get Studied
nodes.claim: The distribution of scientific attention across possible objects of study is shaped less by their importance than by how cheap each one is to measure. Subjects whose measurement is expensive stay unstudied, and the resulting knowledge base is systematically skewed toward the tractable.

nodes.title: Mechanization Lowers the Cost of a Craft Rather Than Raising It
nodes.claim: New production methods - milling, casting, robotic carving - cut the labour required per unit of an ornamental good, so a craft's decline need not reflect rising input costs at all.

nodes.title: Mechanizing a Bottleneck Step Multiplies Whole-System Throughput
nodes.claim: Automating the single slowest step in a process multiplies the throughput of the whole system and drives down unit cost.

nodes.title: Misdiagnosed Crises Produce Perverse Policy
nodes.claim: When the cause of a crisis is misdiagnosed, the "lessons learned" push policy in exactly the wrong direction — institutions built to prevent a recurrence end up entrenching the real underlying problem.

nodes.title: Mismatch Between Evolved Minds and Modern Environments
nodes.claim: Psychological systems adapted to ancestral environments can produce harmful outcomes in modern contexts without being dysfunctional. The system is working as selected; the environment it was tuned to no longer exists.

nodes.title: Missing Complementary Infrastructure Forces Costlier Production
nodes.claim: Absent a needed piece of complementary infrastructure, a product must be re-engineered to work without it, adding manufacturing steps and raising unit cost precisely in the markets least able to pay.

nodes.title: Mixed Traffic Forces Capacity-Sapping Redundancy
nodes.claim: Running different service types over shared track and platforms forces the whole system to operate far below its theoretical maximum, because delays on one service propagate to the others and must be absorbed by slack.

nodes.title: Models Are Sensitive to Unknowable Parameters
nodes.claim: Complex predictive models (e.g. climate integrated-assessment models) can be driven to almost any conclusion by the choice of a few deeply uncertain parameters. Their real value is in revealing what outcomes are sensitive to, not in producing a trustworthy point forecast.

nodes.title: Moderate Engagement in Risk Outperforms Both Extremes in Status Competition
nodes.claim: In status contests that reward willingness to bear risk, individuals who engage with some moderation systematically outperform both those who never engage at all and those who engage most intensely — an inverted-U relationship between risk engagement and payoff, not a monotonic "more is better" one.

nodes.title: Molecular Complexity Resists Synthesis
nodes.claim: The harder a product is to specify and assemble molecule-by-molecule, the longer an animal that already makes the whole mixture remains the cheapest route.

nodes.title: Monopsony Buyers and Locked-In Suppliers Leave No One to Champion Innovation
nodes.claim: In a market where a small number of local monopsonists buy from long-contracted suppliers, neither side has a payoff from introducing a new technology: the buyer bears the risk without competitive pressure to take it, and the supplier's margin is protected by the existing contract and often threatened by the improvement. The result is a market with no natural champion for change, distinct from one where change is opposed.

nodes.title: Moral Discomfort Is Not Evidence That a Behavior Is Unnatural
nodes.claim: Feeling bad about an act does not show that the act is foreign to our evolved repertoire. Where a behavior requires modeling a victim's mind, the discomfort and the competence are produced by the same machinery — so the guilt is evidence that the behavior is old, not that it is new.

nodes.title: Moral Progress via Technological Substitution
nodes.claim: Technologies that remove the need for moral tradeoffs enable moral progress without requiring moral improvement.

nodes.title: Moral Signaling Dominates Private Ethical Behavior
nodes.claim: People adopt moral behaviors primarily to signal identity to others, not to minimize harm in private.

nodes.title: Multiple Transmission Routes Make Single-Vector Control Insufficient
nodes.claim: A pathogen with more than one transmission route cannot be eliminated by targeting a single vector, so interventions aimed at the primary carrier leave a residual channel open.

nodes.title: Mystery and Distance Enable Projection
nodes.claim: People invest longing in an object only when given partial information; too much detail breaks the spell by replacing the imagined ideal with a specific, flawed reality.

nodes.title: Naming and Categorizing Is a Technology
nodes.claim: Giving a practice a name and a category is itself a technology: it bundles dispersed ideas into a memorable unit that can be transmitted, taught, and built upon — enabling "meta-recipes" and rules that generate new instances.

nodes.title: Narrative Selects for Dystopia
nodes.claim: The structure of storytelling biases cultural depictions of the future toward dystopia: a gripping plot needs danger and conflict, which a genuinely utopian world cannot supply — so popular imagination of technology skews pessimistic even absent any hostility to it.

nodes.title: Naturally Occurring Human Mutations De-Risk Drug Targets
nodes.claim: A benign inherited condition that mimics a drug's action provides natural evidence that chronically inhibiting the target is safe over a lifetime.

nodes.title: Near-Term Visible Damage Drives Faster Policy Response
nodes.claim: Environmental problems whose harm is happening now and can be seen get acted on; problems whose worst harm arrives after the decision-makers are gone do not, regardless of the relative size of the two harms.

nodes.title: Neighborhood Environment Causally Shapes Life Outcomes
nodes.claim: Moving disadvantaged households to lower-poverty, lower-crime areas improves mental health, education, employment, and earnings, showing that place itself is a treatment rather than merely a correlate of outcomes.

nodes.title: Neighboring Jurisdictions Copy Restrictions to Deflect Displaced Development
nodes.claim: When one jurisdiction restricts development, the demand does not disappear — it moves to the next jurisdiction, which then adopts the same restriction to protect itself. Restriction therefore propagates outward as a defensive chain reaction until an entire region is closed, even though no actor intended a regional policy.

nodes.title: Network Goods Need a Non-Network Stepping Stone
nodes.claim: A good whose value to any user depends on other users already having it cannot bootstrap itself from zero by its own payoff. Its adoption must be seeded by some prior capacity or practice that was worth having for reasons independent of the network — otherwise the first adopters face a positive cost and no benefit.

nodes.title: Network Value Rises With Each Additional Node
nodes.claim: A shared network good becomes cheaper and more viable per user as more users connect, because fixed costs amortise and utilisation rises with each node.

nodes.title: New Clusters Favor Blank-Slate Locations
nodes.claim: New industries tend to seed their clusters not in the largest established cities but in smaller, less-encumbered locations that can act as a relative blank slate — tight enough for stakeholders to share prototypes and ideas, and free enough to grow a distinct culture around the new field.

nodes.title: New Forms Inherit the Shapes of Old Ones
nodes.claim: New materials and technologies characteristically retain the forms of the predecessors they replace, long after the original functional reason for those forms has gone — a skeuomorphic pattern visible across the history of design.

nodes.title: New Goods Enter Indices After Their Fastest Price Declines
nodes.claim: Administrative lag in adding new products to an index means the index misses the early, steepest phase of their price fall, biasing the aggregate upward until they are belatedly included.

nodes.title: New Knowledge Concentrates Near Existing Knowledge
nodes.claim: Researchers preferentially build on findings close to what they already know, so discoveries that require combining distant fields are systematically underexplored.

nodes.title: New Reproductive Technologies Face Recurring Moral Resistance
nodes.claim: Technologies that touch reproduction and the body meet strong, recurring moral resistance — grounded in the near-universal treatment of motherhood and fertility as sacred — which predictably delays their adoption before they are later accepted as ordinary goods.

nodes.title: New Road Capacity Induces Its Own Demand
nodes.claim: Building additional unpriced road capacity to relieve congestion increases the number of trips taken, because travel on a zero-priced good expands to meet available supply; without demand-side pricing, added capacity can leave congestion unchanged or even worsen it rather than relieving it.

nodes.title: New Supply Absorbs Demand Rather Than Attracting It
nodes.claim: New development is a way of housing incoming demand, not the cause of it; blocking construction does not remove the demand, only redirects it onto the existing stock.

nodes.title: Niche Demand Pulls Dormant Products Back Into Supply
nodes.claim: A small, persistent, sophisticated demand can be enough to make importers and producers reintroduce a discontinued or obscure input, which then scales as it finds a wider market.

nodes.title: NIMBY Support Tracks Who Captures the Gains, Not Ideology
nodes.claim: Opposition or support for density tracks whether the deciding party captures the gains from it, not their race, class, or cultural politics.

nodes.title: Nonpartisan Framing Lets Advocacy Coalitions Recruit Across the Aisle
nodes.claim: Reframing a contested issue as non-ideological — intergenerational, pro-opportunity — lets an advocacy group build support on both left and right without alienating either.

nodes.title: Normative Prohibition, Not Technical Ignorance, Can Block Adoption
nodes.claim: A practice can remain rare for centuries even though the technique is free, simple, and universally known, because a moral authority proscribes it. Adoption then jumps not when the technology improves or cheapens but when the authority's capacity to enforce the prohibition weakens.

nodes.title: Obscure Publication Venue Suppresses a Finding's Reach
nodes.claim: Where a finding is published, not just its content, determines whether it reaches the readers who could use it.

nodes.title: Off-Books Public Corporations Can Borrow Cheaply and Pay for Talent
nodes.claim: Delivering through a state-backed public corporation kept off the government's books lets a project borrow cheaply while escaping civil-service pay scales to hire top talent.

nodes.title: On-the-Job Training Can Substitute for Formal Schooling
nodes.claim: Where skills are acquired mainly by doing, apprenticeship and workplace training can build industrial human capital as effectively as formal schooling -- so a nation's weakness in formal education need not imply a weak workforce.

nodes.title: Open Data and Code Compound Scientific Returns
nodes.claim: When data and analysis code are shared openly in curated, machine-readable repositories, each contribution compounds: later researchers reuse results instead of rediscovering them, and entirely unforeseen projects become possible by recombining existing data.

nodes.title: Open Publication Accelerates a Field That Secrecy Stalls
nodes.claim: Publishing methods in reproducible detail lets others replicate and extend the work, converting a stalled line of inquiry into a rapidly advancing field, whereas secrecy - whether corporate or state-imposed - does the reverse even to the secret-keeper.

nodes.title: Open-Ended Safety Standards Absorb All Productivity Gains
nodes.claim: A safety standard defined relative to what is achievable, rather than against a fixed absolute threshold, converts every efficiency improvement into additional safety spending instead of lower cost. The technology can never get cheaper no matter how much better it gets, because the standard moves with it.

nodes.title: Operating Near Fiscal Limits Erodes Crisis Resilience
nodes.claim: A government can run perpetual deficits while r < g, but the closer it operates to its maximum sustainable primary deficit, the less headroom it retains to respond to the next crisis — so spending near the fiscal limit is itself a reduction in resilience, even when currently affordable.

nodes.title: Opt-Out Rights Let Beneficiaries Drive Reform a Weak State Cannot Enforce
nodes.claim: Where a state lacks capacity to impose change directly, granting individuals a legal option to exit an institution lets self-interested actors carry out the reform themselves.

nodes.title: Opt-Outs at the Smallest Scale Prevent Local Objections from Becoming General Restrictions
nodes.claim: When people who object to something near them have no small-scale way to prevent it, they reach for the largest lever available and impose a restriction on everyone. Giving them a cheap, formal veto over their own immediate area confines the objection to where it originates and protects the general rule from it.

nodes.title: Originality Is an Optional Virtue
